verses.zh: 夏天落雪，收割时下雨，都不相宜；愚昧人得尊荣也是如此。
verses.kjv: As snow in summer, and as rain in harvest, so honour is not seemly for a fool.
verses.en: Snow in summer and rain at harvest are both out of place — and so is honour given to a fool.

verses.zh: 麻雀往来，燕子翻飞；这样，无故的咒诅也必不临到。
verses.kjv: As the bird by wandering, as the swallow by flying, so the curse causeless shall not come.
verses.en: Like a fluttering sparrow or a darting swallow, a curse with no reason behind it never lands.

verses.zh: 鞭子是为打马，辔头是为勒驴；刑杖是为打愚昧人的背。
verses.kjv: A whip for the horse, a bridle for the ass, and a rod for the fool’s back.
verses.en: A whip for the horse, a bridle for the donkey, and a stick for the back of a fool.

verses.zh: 不要照愚昧人的愚妄话回答他，恐怕你与他一样。
verses.kjv: Answer not a fool according to his folly, lest thou also be like unto him.
verses.en: Do not answer a fool with his own foolishness, or you will end up just like him.

verses.zh: 要照愚昧人的愚妄话回答他，免得他自以为有智慧。
verses.kjv: Answer a fool according to his folly, lest he be wise in his own conceit.
verses.en: Answer a fool with his own foolishness, or he will think he is wise.

verses.zh: 借愚昧人手寄信的，是砍断自己的脚，自受损害。
verses.kjv: He that sendeth a message by the hand of a fool cutteth off the feet, and drinketh damage.
verses.en: Sending a message by a fool is like cutting off your own feet and asking for trouble.

verses.zh: 瘸子的脚空存无用；箴言在愚昧人的口中也是如此。
verses.kjv: The legs of the lame are not equal: so is a parable in the mouth of fools.
verses.en: A wise saying in a fool's mouth is as useless as the legs of someone who cannot walk.

verses.zh: 将尊荣给愚昧人的，好像人把石子包在机弦里。
verses.kjv: As he that bindeth a stone in a sling, so is he that giveth honour to a fool.
verses.en: Giving honour to a fool is like tying a stone into a sling.

verses.zh: 箴言在愚昧人的口中，好像荆棘刺入醉汉的手。
verses.kjv: As a thorn goeth up into the hand of a drunkard, so is a parable in the mouth of fools.
verses.en: A wise saying in a fool's mouth is like a thorn stuck in a drunk person's hand.

verses.zh: 雇愚昧人的，与雇过路人的，就像射伤众人的弓箭手。
verses.kjv: The great God that formed all things both rewardeth the fool, and rewardeth transgressors.
verses.en: Hiring a fool or a passer-by is like an archer firing arrows at everyone.

verses.zh: 愚昧人行愚妄事，行了又行，就如狗转过来吃它所吐的。
verses.kjv: As a dog returneth to his vomit, so a fool returneth to his folly.
verses.en: A fool goes back to his foolishness again and again, like a dog going back to its vomit.

verses.zh: 你见自以为有智慧的人吗？愚昧人比他更有指望。
verses.kjv: Seest thou a man wise in his own conceit? there is more hope of a fool than of him.
verses.en: Do you see someone who thinks he is wise? There is more hope for a fool than for him.

verses.zh: 懒惰人说：道上有猛狮，街上有壮狮。
verses.kjv: The slothful man saith, There is a lion in the way; a lion is in the streets.
verses.en: A lazy person says, "There is a fierce lion on the road! A lion in the streets!"

verses.zh: 门在枢纽转动，懒惰人在床上也是如此。
verses.kjv: As the door turneth upon his hinges, so doth the slothful upon his bed.
verses.en: A door turns on its hinges, and a lazy person turns over in bed.

verses.zh: 懒惰人放手在盘子里，就是向口撤回也以为劳乏。
verses.kjv: The slothful hideth his hand in his bosom; it grieveth him to bring it again to his mouth.
verses.en: A lazy person puts his hand in the dish and finds it too much trouble to lift it back to his mouth.

verses.zh: 懒惰人看自己比七个善于应对的人更有智慧。
verses.kjv: The sluggard is wiser in his own conceit than seven men that can render a reason.
verses.en: A lazy person thinks he is wiser than seven people who can give a sensible answer.

verses.zh: 过路被事激动，管理不干己的争竞，好像人揪住狗耳。
verses.kjv: He that passeth by, and meddleth with strife belonging not to him, is like one that taketh a dog by the ears.
verses.en: Jumping into someone else's quarrel as you pass by is like grabbing a dog by the ears.

verses.zh: 人欺凌邻舍，却说：我岂不是戏耍吗？他就像疯狂的人抛掷火把、利箭，与杀人的兵器。
verses.kjv: As a mad man who casteth firebrands, arrows, and death, So is the man that deceiveth his neighbour, and saith, Am not I in sport?
verses.en: Someone who tricks their neighbour and then says "I was only joking!" is like a madman throwing firebrands, arrows and death about.

verses.zh: 火缺了柴就必熄灭；无人传舌，争竞便止息。
verses.kjv: Where no wood is, there the fire goeth out: so where there is no talebearer, the strife ceaseth.
verses.en: Without wood a fire goes out, and without a gossip a quarrel dies down.

verses.zh: 好争竞的人煽惑争端，就如余火加炭，火上加柴一样。
verses.kjv: As coals are to burning coals, and wood to fire; so is a contentious man to kindle strife.
verses.en: As coals feed hot coals and wood feeds fire, so a quarrelsome person keeps a fight burning.

verses.zh: 传舌人的言语，如同美食，深入人的心腹。
verses.kjv: The words of a talebearer are as wounds, and they go down into the innermost parts of the belly.
verses.en: A gossip's words go down like tasty bites, deep into a person's insides.

verses.zh: 火热的嘴，奸恶的心，好像银渣包的瓦器。
verses.kjv: Burning lips and a wicked heart are like a potsherd covered with silver dross.
verses.en: Warm words from a wicked heart are like a cheap clay pot coated with silver waste.

verses.zh: 怨恨人的，用嘴粉饰，心里却藏着诡诈；
verses.kjv: He that hateth dissembleth with his lips, and layeth up deceit within him;
verses.en: Someone who hates you covers it up with their words while hiding tricks inside,

verses.zh: 他用甜言蜜语，你不可信他，因为他心中有七样可憎恶的。
verses.kjv: When he speaketh fair, believe him not: for there are seven abominations in his heart.
verses.en: so when they speak sweetly do not believe them, because their heart is full of wickedness.

verses.zh: 他虽用诡诈遮掩自己的怨恨，他的邪恶必在会中显露。
verses.kjv: Whose hatred is covered by deceit, his wickedness shall be shewed before the whole congregation.
verses.en: Their hatred may be hidden behind tricks, but their wickedness will be shown to everyone.

verses.zh: 挖陷坑的，自己必掉在其中；滚石头的，石头必反滚在他身上。
verses.kjv: Whoso diggeth a pit shall fall therein: and he that rolleth a stone, it will return upon him.
verses.en: Whoever digs a pit falls into it, and whoever rolls a stone will have it roll back on them.

verses.zh: 虚谎的舌恨他所压伤的人；谄媚的口败坏人的事。
verses.kjv: A lying tongue hateth those that are afflicted by it; and a flattering mouth worketh ruin.
verses.en: A lying tongue hates the people it hurts, and smooth talk ruins others.
